function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure, provided in kilopascals (kPa) or atmospheres (atm). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), pure water freezes at roughly **–20 °C**.  

This value comes from the water phase diagram: as pressure drops below atmospheric, the solid–liquid equilibrium line shifts to lower temperatures. At 10 kPa the melting/freezing point is about –20 °C (the exact value depends slightly on the purity of the water, but –20 °C is the accepted figure for standard laboratory conditions).
